title: Triplet Network-Based DNA Encoding for Enhanced Similarity Image Retrieval
problem: Designing efficient encoding and retrieval methods for image data within DNA storage systems to enable fast and accurate similarity-based image search.
motivation: DNA storage is emerging as an attractive medium for handling large-scale digital data growth, making efficient encoding and search algorithms critical for practical deployment.
method: A triplet network-based encoder learns DNA representations of images optimized for similarity matching. The approach uses CIFAR-100 dataset with triplet loss to train the encoder, enabling efficient retrieval of similar images by comparing encoded DNA sequences.
key_novelty: Applying triplet neural networks to learn DNA-compatible encodings for image similarity retrieval, achieving significantly improved accuracy and training efficiency.
contributions: Introduces image similarity retrieval as an evaluation benchmark for DNA encoder performance
Proposes a triplet network-based DNA encoder architecture for improved image retrieval
Achieves 0.77 accuracy on CIFAR-100, reaching 94% of the theoretical performance upper bound
Demonstrates 16x speedup in training time compared to existing DNA encoders
limitations: Practical scalability to larger datasets and real-world DNA storage system constraints are not discussed.
primary_theme: DNA-based neural encoding for efficient image similarity retrieval
